A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same SURF study. Their complete main texts and appendices, including equations, figures, and tables, are readable and support reliable comparison.

before.justification: V2 reports original surrogate comparisons, three-task benchmarking, concept-count experiments, and adversarial evaluations in Section 6.

after.justification: V4 reports original surrogate comparisons, expanded U-CBEM benchmarking, concept-count experiments, and additional architecture results in Appendix D.

M1.justification: The proposed linear surrogate and MAE/EMD definitions remain unchanged in Equations (9)–(12). V4 explicitly documents restoring the classifier bias before evaluation; this clarifies implementation without establishing a newly introduced algorithmic step.

E1.justification: Caltech-101 classification, CelebA attribute prediction, and UTK-Face age regression remain. However, v2's adversarial-image scenario, including Section 6.4 and Appendix C, is removed entirely. The added architectures do not introduce new datasets or tasks.

E2.justification: Table 4 expands the evaluated methods from CDISCO, ICE, CRAFT, C-SHAP, and MCD to include HU-MCD and SAE. HU-MCD participates in ResNet-50 classification, while SAE participates in all three tasks; both also enter Figure 2. The measure-over-measure comparator set remains unchanged.

E3.justification: V4 revises the reported ResNet training setup to include label smoothing, adds VGG11 and InceptionV3 evaluations, introduces FLOPs as a surrogate-complexity metric, and extends Figure 2's maximum concept count from 15 to 30. These alter the evaluation design, although the principal dataset splits remain unchanged.

E4.justification: The complete PGD robustness analysis is removed. The retained parsimony analysis is expanded with HU-MCD and SAE, examining oscillation, plateauing, and the crossover between MCD and HU-MCD as concept counts increase.

E5.justification: Both versions average the measure-over-measure results over 10 seeds. V4 removes the adversarial experiment's one-sided paired t-test at p < 0.01 and its significance-filtered reporting, without adding replacement uncertainty reporting.

E6.justification: Table 3 and Table 4's classification results are extensively revised: for example, MCD's classification MAE/EMD changes from 1.42/0.079 to 2.60/0.426. Because the reported classification training setup also changes, this is not a controlled deterioration. HU-MCD, SAE, and additional-architecture results are added, while adversarial results disappear. Existing CelebA scores and CDISCO's age MAE of 32.6 are retained.

T1.justification: Appendix B.3 adds analytical FLOP-count expressions for the three surrogates, including 2KC for SURF. V4 also qualifies the linear-layer identity as holding up to the bias term. The central faithfulness definitions and surrogate derivation otherwise remain unchanged; no new theorem or proof is introduced.

C1.justification: The central SURF and comprehensive-benchmark contributions remain. V4 removes adversarial robustness from the advertised contributions and centers the downstream contribution on concept-count selection. Its revised benchmark conclusion also removes the exception previously made for MCD.

C2.justification: V4 adds substantial interpretation of SAE faithfulness metrics in Appendix A, explicitly explains why SURF does not extend to nonlinear intermediate-layer explanations, and stresses the need for separate interpretability assessment. It also qualifies completeness guarantees through their dependence on uninterpretable residuals. The adversarial-vulnerability discussion is removed.

D1.justification: V4 replaces the promised code release with a release statement and repository link. It adds bias-restoration details, the timm model source, FLOP-counting conventions, and HU-MCD/SAE implementation information, including Overcomplete and the SAE dictionary/top-K configuration. The removed adversarial experiment's implementation details also disappear.

R1.justification: V4 incorporates HU-MCD and multiple SAE research lines into its positioning. New Appendix A compares SURF with reconstruction, downstream-loss, masking, and plausibility metrics, presenting SURF as complementary to SAE evaluation. This substantially expands the prior-work discussion beyond citation updates.

P1.justification: The abstract, introduction, framework exposition, and conclusion are extensively rewritten. The separate concept-bottleneck-model subsection is compressed, deletion measures are consistently framed as proxies, metric terminology is standardized, and the supplementary material is reorganized around new SAE discussion and additional benchmarks.

P2.justification: The compact SURF pipeline figure is replaced by a full-width comparison of surrogate and deletion frameworks. Table 1 is redesigned, Table 3 gains FLOPs, Table 4 gains methods, and Figure 2 is replotted with additional curves and a wider range. The adversarial table is removed; a different Table 5 presents additional architectures in the appendix.

improvement.justification: The HU-MCD/SAE comparisons and VGG11/InceptionV3 results strengthen the central benchmark, while explicit applicability limits and improved implementation and code-access documentation make the work easier to assess. The gain is limited: the core measure and validation design remain, and adversarial evidence is lost. Revised classification settings also prevent treating changed scores as controlled performance improvements.
